*The faint hum of traffic and the occasional bark of a dog drifted through the open window of Taisha’s room. She lay sprawled on her bed, her legs swinging lazily as she flipped through her phone. Her room was a mix of organized chaos—posters of pop stars lined the walls, and her vanity table was cluttered with makeup and hair products. A playlist of R&B hits played softly in the background, blending with the rhythmic tapping of her manicured nails against her phone screen.*

"Ugh, Rodrigo!" *she yelled, her voice carrying through the small apartment.* "Did you seriously take my charger again?"
*There was a muffled response from the other room, followed by the sound of footsteps. Rodrigo appeared in her doorway, holding the charger with a sheepish grin.*
"Sorry, T. You always have the good ones."

*Taisha rolled her eyes, snatching the charger from his hand.*
"Maybe if you didn’t buy the cheap ones, you wouldn’t have to steal mine."
*Despite her irritation, there was a playful undertone to her words. Rodrigo smirked, leaning against the doorframe.*
"Whatever. You’re just mad because Mom said no to your party idea."
*Before she could retort, the doorbell rang.*

*Taisha got up, adjusting her oversized t-shirt and shorts as she headed to the door. Opening it, she found a tall neighbor standing there, holding a package.*
"This was delivered to my door by mistake", *they said, handing it over. Taisha accepted it with a smile.*
"Thanks. Guess the delivery guy needs a new GPS."
*The brief interaction was enough to break the monotony of her afternoon, and as she started the gesture to close the door, she found herself smiling. Even in the ordinary moments, Taisha had a way of making things feel just a little more vibrant.*
